about: Bengaluru-headquartered IT/ITeS solutions company with a 26-year track record building and running digital platforms for Government bodies and enterprises in healthcare, electronic governance, and telecom and broadband. It works mainly through turnkey, tender-based projects, using sub-contractors for delivery. It has executed 103+ projects in India and overseas (Qatar, UAE, Nigeria and others) and reported FY26 revenue of about Rs 450 crore.
sector: IT / IT-enabled services (Government IT systems integration)

objects.purpose: Capex for modernization and redevelopment of existing products (R-Converge, RHES/OP Live, healthcare insurance and RCM)
Funding working capital requirements of the Company
Unidentified acquisitions / strategic initiatives and general corporate purposes (capped at 35% of gross proceeds)

promoters.background: Dr. Nambiar (MD and CEO, 26+ years in IT) holds 50.58% alone. Prasaktha Nambiar (22+ years in training and development) and Martin Chacko (35+ years in IT) are whole-time directors. No promoter shares are pledged.

concentration.note: Top 10 customers were 89.36% of FY26 revenue (92.68% FY25, 84.54% FY24); top 3 were 57.93% and top 5 were 75.55% in FY26. Top customers include RailTel, TCIL and SEEPZ SEZ Authority. Electronic governance was 68.39% of FY26 revenue.

litigation_note: Contingent liabilities at Mar-26 include Rs 30.15 cr bank guarantees, Rs 21.48 cr performance/surety bonds, Rs 4.49 cr civil litigations and tax disputes. Pending matters include a contempt petition by sub-contractor Advantage SB Communications (Bombay HC, unquantified), a Rs 1.71 cr CSA Consultants arbitration, and a Rs 2.52 cr Galmax arbitration claim.
strengths: 26-year track record delivering large government IT projects, with CMMI Level 5 and ISO 27001 certifications.
Revenue grew from Rs 271 cr in FY24 to Rs 450 cr in FY26 (28.8% CAGR); PAT grew from Rs 29 cr to Rs 43 cr.
Order book of Rs 1,183 cr at Mar-26 (Rs 1,205 cr at June 2026) is about 2.6 times FY26 revenue.
Three verticals (healthcare, e-governance, telecom/broadband) plus new AI and power-utility projects widen the pipeline.
Repeat clients rose from 61% to 74% of clients served between FY24 and FY26.
High returns: FY26 ROCE 28.79% and RoNW 30.23%; debt-to-equity fell to 0.23.
In-house software products (R-Converge, RHES, health insurance engine) and overseas delivery in Qatar and other countries.
Fresh issue earmarks Rs 124 cr for working capital, which could reduce reliance on partners and borrowings.

risks.title: Heavy dependence on Government tenders
risks.detail: Government clients gave 89.41% of FY26 revenue (91.34% FY25) and 86.28% of the order book. Bid win ratio was only 13.95% in FY26 (6 of 43 bids).

risks.title: Customer concentration
risks.detail: Top 10 customers were 89.36% of FY26 revenue and top 3 were 57.93%. Losing one major customer such as RailTel or TCIL would hit revenue hard.

risks.title: Weak cash conversion and heavy receivables
risks.detail: Operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -12.10 cr in FY26 despite Rs 43 cr PAT. Trade receivables plus contract assets were 63.27% of total assets; contract assets rose to Rs 153.80 cr.

risks.title: Heavy reliance on sub-contractors
risks.detail: Sub-contracting and technical fees were 78.92% of total expenses in FY26; 41% of revenue came from projects executed through sub-contractors. A sub-contractor default on an SBI ATM project led to arbitration and a Rs 4.05 cr loan extended to it.

risks.title: Sector concentration in e-governance
risks.detail: Electronic governance was 68.39% of FY26 revenue and 58.40% of the order book; any cut in government IT spending would hurt growth.

risks.title: Promoter-linked related party dealings
risks.detail: Related-party transactions were Rs 43.08 cr (9.57% of FY26 revenue) and Rs 51.74 cr (13.29%) in FY25, including promoter loans converted to equity at Rs 70 per share and buyback payments to promoters in FY25.

risks.title: Pending litigation and contingent liabilities
risks.detail: Contingent liabilities include Rs 30.15 cr bank guarantees, Rs 21.48 cr surety bonds, disputed GST and service tax, and sub-contractor arbitration claims of Rs 1.71 cr and Rs 2.52 cr.

risks.title: Order book may not convert to revenue
risks.detail: Order book fell from Rs 1,477 cr at Mar-24 to Rs 1,183 cr at Mar-26, and projects can be cancelled, delayed or re-scoped. Use of proceeds is not bank-appraised and up to 35% may go to unidentified acquisitions and general purposes.

notes: FY26 restated consolidated financials (Rs million converted to Rs crore); Q1FY27 stub not in arrays. Prospectus: price band Rs 123-130, fresh issue 16,800,000 shares (Rs 218.40 cr at cap), no OFS; pre-issue shares 47,471,757, post-issue 64,271,757. P/E 13.73 at cap price (12.99 at floor) on FY26 EPS; post-issue P/E not stated. Promoter post-issue holding 62.59% (37.36+13.00+12.23). Net worth is owners' equity (excludes NCI). Borrowings exclude lease liabilities. Cash and bank is cash plus other bank balances. EBITDA per document definition (excludes other income). Operating cash flow reconstructed from a garbled table. ROE set equal to RoNW (text also cites ROE 29.98% for FY26). Objects: capex 12.86, working capital 124.00, inorganic growth and general corporate purposes 55.13 (Rs cr); issue expenses Rs 26.42 cr.
